data.title: Etanercept
data.summary: Biologicals · TNF-α inhibitor — fusion protein of TNF receptor 2 (p75) with the Fc portion of IgG1
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Biologicals_

**Class:** TNF-α inhibitor — fusion protein of TNF receptor 2 (p75) with the Fc portion of IgG1

## Mechanism of action
- Acts as a soluble decoy receptor binding TNF-α (and lymphotoxin-α), preventing it from activating cell receptors
- Does not lyse TNF-bearing cells (unlike monoclonal antibodies) — less granulomatous infection risk

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Moderate–severe plaque psoriasis (adults and children ≥4 years), psoriatic arthritis
- Off-label: hidradenitis (weak), pyoderma gangrenosum, SJS/TEN (single dose in trials), sarcoidosis (ineffective)

## Dose & formulations
- Psoriasis: 50 mg SC twice weekly for 12 weeks, then 50 mg once weekly; children 0.8 mg/kg weekly

## Adverse effects
- Injection-site reactions (common), upper respiratory infections
- Serious infections; TB reactivation (lower than monoclonals but still screen); hepatitis B reactivation
- Demyelinating disease, drug-induced lupus, worsening heart failure
- Paradoxical psoriasis (palmoplantar pustular), lymphoma risk (small)

## Contraindications
- Active serious infection, untreated latent TB, multiple sclerosis/demyelination, NYHA III–IV heart failure, live vaccines

## Drug interactions
- Do not combine with other biologics or anakinra/abatacept (serious infections)

## Monitoring
- TB screening (IGRA) before and yearly; hepatitis B/C, HIV; CBC/LFT periodically

## Pregnancy & lactation
Low placental transfer (Fc fusion protein) — can be used if needed; avoid live vaccines in infants for 6 months if exposed late.

## Viva points
- Receptor fusion protein — decoy for TNF
- TNF inhibitors: screen for TB, avoid in demyelination and severe heart failure
- Paradoxical psoriasis with TNF inhibitors

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.26 (TNF inhibitors); Khopkar (Immunobiologicals). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
